Its three callers are the oracle's four referrers modulo one level: ecs::EntityWorld::Update tail-jumps to it with rdi = its own this, 0x75b04b0 (= EntityWorld::Unload; it calls DeactivateSystemInternal 0x3659120) calls it, and 0x3817fd0 tail-jumps the same way, called from ecl::EocClient::Load 0x4013620 and from 0x365d030 off ServerWorker::DoWork 0x2afbe70. 0x3817fd0 is also upstream's BinaryMappings.xml signature for this name read back: the bytes it puts after the call (mov rbx,[world+0x30]; mov eax,[world+0x3c]; imul rdi, rax, 0xf8) are that function's whole loop. Two more readings say rdi is an ecs::EntityWorld in this build's measured layout: at 0x2487096 the spilled rdi (from [rsp+0x60]) is read at +0x300, +0x348 and +0x350 in one breath -- Executor, Cache and Settings.JobPriority, the three offsets EntitySystem.h's Linux asserts carry -- and they are handed to the inlined ECBExecutor::Execute(ImmediateWorldCache&, EWorkerThreadBatchPriority); and the caller 0x365d030 calls 0x3817fd0 with rdi = [EoCServer + 0x288], the server world's known offset.
